item.title: Paper: TS-RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation for Time Series Forecasting
item.description: This paper introduces a retrieval-augmented approach for time series forecasting, allowing models to improve accuracy by referencing similar historical patterns from external datasets.

item.title: Paper: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
item.description: The authors created a multi-agent system that automates clinical feature engineering by linking electronic health records to medical guidelines, significantly reducing manual data preparation time.

item.title: Paper: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
item.description: This study evaluates and improves how LLMs handle complex, rule-heavy professional documents, providing a framework for automating quality reviews of technical standards.

item.title: Paper: QuanTiMedAI: Quantum-Enhanced Time-Series Model guided by Agentic AI for Cardiac Arrest Mortality Prediction
item.description: This framework combines quantum-inspired computing with agentic AI to better predict cardiac arrest mortality by analyzing the full temporal progression of patient health data.

item.title: Paper: Spoken Function Calling: A New Perspective on Spoken Language Understanding for Large Audio Language Models
item.description: This paper introduces a structured approach for audio-based AI agents to execute specific functions directly from speech, improving their ability to handle open-domain tasks without complex manual rules.

item.title: Paper: The Effect of Perceived Race and Gender on Police Language Use: Experimental Evidence from VR Simulations
item.description: Researchers used VR simulations to measure how police officers' language patterns change based on the perceived race and gender of virtual characters, providing a causal framework for bias analysis.

item.title: Paper: Teaching Nemotron Greek: Mining a Corpus, Adapting Retrieval, and Grounding Generation for Modern Greek across Specialist Domains
item.description: The authors adapted a retrieval-augmented generation stack for Modern Greek, demonstrating that simple keyword-based methods often outperform complex multilingual dense retrievers in specialized domains.

item.title: Paper: DASyR-LLM: Domain-Aware Symbolic Regression with LLMs for Kinetic Model Discovery
item.description: This framework integrates LLMs into symbolic regression to ensure that data-driven kinetic models for chemical engineering remain physically plausible and scientifically interpretable.

item.title: Paper: WorldCup Arena: Prospective, Leakage-Free Evaluation of Frontier LLMs on a Live Tournament
item.description: The authors evaluated LLM forecasting accuracy using live World Cup matches to prevent data leakage from training sets, offering a reliable way to test real-world predictive reasoning.

item.title: Paper: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent
item.description: This framework improves multimodal agents by forcing them to prioritize video analysis over text-based search, reducing reliance on outdated internal memory for complex tasks.

item.title: Paper: MultiGlobeQA: A Multilingual and Globally Diverse Benchmark for Geospatial Reasoning
item.description: This multilingual benchmark helps data scientists measure how well LLMs handle real-world geospatial reasoning, such as calculating distances and spatial relationships across diverse global regions.

item.title: Paper: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?
item.description: This framework tests whether LLM agents can actually improve their performance over time by learning and reusing skills across increasingly difficult, interconnected tasks.

item.title: Paper: Why Large Language Models Fail at Tabular Prediction
item.description: Researchers analyzed why LLMs struggle with tabular data, helping data scientists understand when to stick with traditional gradient-boosted trees instead of forcing language models into predictive tasks.

item.title: Paper: Agentic Incident Response through Digital Twin-Enhanced Multiscale Planning
item.description: This paper introduces a digital twin framework to automate security incident responses, providing a more reliable and actionable alternative to manual, playbook-driven cybersecurity operations.

item.title: Paper: Bridging Artificial Intelligence and Power Systems Education Using a Hands-On Executable Framework
item.description: The authors propose an engineering-grounded AI framework for power systems, ensuring that AI models adhere to domain-specific physical rules rather than relying on black-box predictions.

item.title: Paper: The Condition-Number Barrier in Sparse Least Squares
item.description: This theoretical work proves that the condition number limits the accuracy of sparse least-squares optimization, providing practitioners with a fundamental bound on algorithm performance.

item.title: Paper: AMTFV: Agentic Mathematical Tool-Flow Verification for LLM Self-Correction
item.description: This framework improves LLM mathematical accuracy by decoupling problem modeling from code execution, allowing agents to verify steps through a structured tool-flow process.

item.title: Paper: Differentially Private Nonparametric Modal Learning with Applications to Regression and Clustering
item.description: The authors introduce a privacy-preserving method for identifying data clusters and regression modes, providing a robust way to analyze sensitive datasets without compromising individual privacy.

item.title: Paper: The Parts Are Greater Than the Sum: Automated Task Sequencing for Efficient Training of Multi-Policy LLMs
item.description: This approach optimizes multi-task LLM fine-tuning by organizing adapter paths to prevent interference and catastrophic forgetting when training models on diverse, sequential tasks.

item.title: Paper: DungeonBench: A Benchmark for Rules-Rich Tactical Reasoning in Dungeons & Dragons Combat
item.description: DungeonBench provides a new evaluation framework for testing how well AI models handle complex, rule-heavy tactical decision-making in simulated environments.
